You can change all the characters in a string to lowercase using the lower() commands. Below shows an example: string = "ABC" string = string.lower() print(string) <- this will display "abc"

Create a program that asks you to enter a string and displays it in lowercase format.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input FUN

Funny

FuNniEr

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input string: FUN fun

Example 2 Input string: Funny funny

Example 3 Input string: FuNniEr funnier

You can change all the characters in a string to uppercase using the upper() commands. Below shows an example: string = "abc" string = string.upper() print(string) <- this will display "ABC"

Create a program that asks you to enter a string and displays it in uppercase format.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input FUN

Funny

FuNniEr

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input string: FUN FUN

Example 2 Input string: Funny FUNNY

Example 3 Input string: FuNniEr FUNNIER

Create a program that does the following: 1. asks you to enter the species and colour of an animal. 2. create a variable sentence, in the format: "your species is colour in colour" (e.g. if "cat" and "white" are entered, it will display "your cat is white in colour") 3. display sentence.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input dog brown

Fish Gold

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Animal's species: dog Animal's colour: brown your dog is brown in colour

Example 2 Animal's species: Fish Animal's colour: Gold your Fish is Gold in colour

Fish 2 Gold
